catalog_quote: The Bagvalal word has a rather peculiar organisation, exemplifying a transition from a non-stress to a stress system. There are three classes of words; words with a strong prominence (normal stress), words with a less pronounced prominence (weak stress) and words with no prominence at all (completely unstressed). The difference in prominence is felt clearly when minimal pairs are compared. In words with strong prominence the stress may fall on any syllable, in words with weak prominence the stress is usually oriented towards the right edge. It falls either on the final heavy syllable or on the prefinal one when the final one is light. Words without any prominence receive a slight intensification of the initial syllable when they occur in isolation. [Kodzasov, carried by StressTyp2].. (2001: 44) identify three nominal accentua…

sources.quote: Bagvalal (Kvanada) is NOT among the 22 surveyed varieties. General statement p.318: 'most Daghestanian languages have a syllabic tonal accent ... all Andic and Tsezic [surveyed] ... In languages with syllabic tone word stress is usually absent (exception: Gigatli Chamalal); phrasal accent goes to the first syllable or to a heavy non-first one (closed or long-vowel syllable)'.

sources.note: The only full primary description of Bagvalal word prosody (three accentual classes, minimal pairs, paradigm mobility, instrumental measurements); our classification rests on a database-carried survey passage and second-hand summaries of exactly these pages; would also settle the weight definition for weak stress (closed vs closed-or-long; record has what counts as heavy: CVC).
